meta.description:
1.1. Background
This Job Safety Training Outline (JSTO) meets the requirements of DAFI 91-202 (The US Air Force Mishap Prevention Program), Chapter 14. It
covers mandatory general safety items as well as work-center-specific hazards for Civil Engineer Electrical Systems personnel. It incorporates
requirements applicable to Dover AFB, the 436th Airlift Wing, and Air Mobility Command (AMC).
1.2. Implementation
The immediate/frontline supervisor must brief this JSTO to all newly assigned military and civilian personnel prior to performing work in the shop or
field. Additional briefings are required whenever new equipment, processes, chemicals, or revised safety/fire/health directives are introduced. Work
center supervisors (NCOICs, Shop Chiefs, Foremen) will review, update, and re-certify this JSTO annually or upon any operational change.
1.3. Mandatory Items
The 10 mandatory safety items outlined in DAFI 91-202, paragraph 14.1, must be briefed and understood by all personnel prior to unsupervised
work.
1.4. Job-Specific Items
Shop-specific training modules based on the mission requirements of the Electrical Systems Shop (CEOFE) must be instructed to the application
level and fully documented prior to performing unsupervised tasks.
1.5. Methods of Documentation
Training completion is documented on the AF Form 55 (Employee Safety and Health Record) or through an approved digital equivalent (e.g., Air
Force Safety Automated System / myLearning). The form requires digital or physical signatures from both the trainee and supervisor and must be
retained in shop records.
meta.jhaNotes:
Aircraft & Flightline Environment (Airfield Electrical & Snow Removal Operations)
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203; AFI 21-101, AMC Sup 1; 436 AW Airfield Driving Instruction; Latest Annual BE Industrial Hygiene
Survey.
Procedures: Strictly observe all flightline and airfield safety rules. When accessing active taxiways or runways (for runway lighting,
PAPI/VASI maintenance, airfield vaults, or snow clearance), maintain two-way radio contact with the Dover Air Traffic Control Tower and
Base Operations/Airfield Management. State exact vehicle call sign, location, and requested access route/runway.
Flightline Speed Limits:
General-purpose vehicles: 15 MPH
Special-purpose vehicles / towing: 10 MPH
Within 50 feet of aircraft: 5 MPH
Aircraft parking ramp: 15 MPH
Vehicle parking areas: 5 MPH
Snow/ice removal equipment: Safe operating speed dictated by surface conditions and visibility.
Seasonal Weather Extremes
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203; 436 AW Severe Weather OIs.
Hazards & Controls: Dover AFB experiences mid-Atlantic extremes—freezing rain, heavy snow, high winds, hurricane/tropical storm force
winds, thunderstorms, lightning (Lightning within 5 nautical miles requires cessation of outside aerial/high-reach and airfield electrical
maintenance), high summer heat index, and sunburn. Dress in authorized layers, hydrate, utilize sunscreen, and seek shelter during
inclement weather advisories.
General Electrical Safety Awareness
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203; AFMAN 32-1065; UFC 3-560-01 (Electrical Safety, O&M); NFPA 70E.
Controls: Recognize and respect electrical hazards including arc flash, arc blast, electrical shock, phase shorts, damaged cable insulation,
and faulty disconnects. Never work on energized circuits without an approved Energized Electrical Work Permit and proper PPE rated for the
incident energy exposure. Inspect tools, extension cords, GFCI devices, and protective equipment prior to every use.
Mechanical Safety & Shop Equipment
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203.
Controls: Follow established safety protocols when operating shop drill presses, conduit benders, pipe threaders, hydraulic knockout sets,
and powered machinery. Ensure all safety guards and interlocks are in place before operation. Wear appropriate eye and hand protection.
Material Handling & Lifting Techniques
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203.
Controls: Lift with the legs, keeping loads close to the body; do not twist during lifting. Utilize mechanical lifting aids (hand trucks, pallet
jacks, hoists, forklift support) for transformers, heavy conduit bundles, switchgear components, and reels of cable. Utilize team lifts for items
exceeding individual lifting limits or awkward dimensions.
Compressed Gas & High-Pressure Elements
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203.
Controls: Secure all compressed gas cylinders (nitrogen, calibration gases) upright with safety chains or approved brackets. Cylinder caps
must remain installed when not connected for use. Never direct compressed gas at skin or clothing. When supporting environmental or
emergency response, review chemical flammability, toxicity, and pressure hazards.
Confined Space Awareness
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203, Chapter 23; 436 AW Confined Space Program.
Shop Policy: The 436 CES Electrical Systems Shop does not operate under a Master Entry Plan (MEP) because entries into electrical
manholes, pull boxes, and vaults are non-routine.
Entry Protocol: Any entry into a permit-required confined space requires prior coordination with Bioenvironmental Engineering (BEE),
436 AW Occupational Safety (SEG), and the Dover Fire Emergency Services (FES). A current AF Form 1024 (Confined Space Entry
Permit) must be completed, signed by all three agencies, and retained on file for one year. Rescue gear (e.g., tripod/winch coordinated with
the WFSM shop) and calibrated atmospheric monitors must be on site and tested prior to breaking the plane of any manhole or vault.
Waste Disposal & Environmental Compliance
Governing Directives: DAFBI 48-101; AFI 90-821; 436 CES Environmental Management Guidelines.
Procedures: Dispose of hazardous wastes (transformer oils, dielectric fluids, degreasers, solvent-soaked rags) strictly per environmental
guidelines. The CEOFE shop maintains universal-waste collection containers for lead-acid/lithium/Ni-Cad batteries, fluorescent lamps, high
pressure sodium (HPS) and metal-halide bulbs, and empty aerosol cans. Keep all waste containers closed, labeled, and dated.
Hazardous Noise
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 48-20; 436 OMRS/Bioenvironmental Engineering Survey.
Controls: Wear approved hearing protection (pre-molded earplugs or sound-attenuating earmuffs) when operating equipment generating 85
dBA or higher (e.g., concrete saws, power tools, large generators, or when working on the flightline near operating C-5M Super Galaxy or C
17 Globemaster III aircraft). Custom or replacement hearing protection is coordinated through Public Health.
Foreign Object Damage (FOD) Prevention
Governing Directives: DAFBI 21-105; 436 AW FOD Prevention Program.
Controls: Strict tool and hardware accountability is mandatory on the flightline and airfield. Conduct 100% foreign object sweeps before
departing airfield vaults, runway/taxiway lighting fixtures, or aircraft parking ramps. Secure all wire clippings, screws, connectors, and tools in
closed tool bags.
Civil Engineer Fall Protection & Elevated Work
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203, Chapter 13 & 14; 29 CFR 1910 / 1926.
Shop Application: Fall protection is mandatory when working at heights of four (4) feet or more in general industry settings or six (6) feet
or more during facility construction/maintenance, including work on utility poles, aerial bucket trucks, scissors lifts, facility roofs, high-bay
hangar light fixtures, and substations.
Controls: Inspect full-body harnesses, shock-absorbing lanyards, self-retracting lifelines (SRLs), and anchor straps prior to use. Personnel
operating bucket trucks or boom lifts must be tied off to approved anchor points 100% of the time while in the basket. Ensure an approved
rescue plan is established before any elevated operation begins.
Walking-Working Surfaces & Housekeeping
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203.
Controls: Keep all aisles, electrical panel clear zones (minimum 36-inch clearance), exit doors, and shop floors free of cords, tools, scrap
metal, oil slicks, and debris. Clean up spills immediately. Report exterior ice/snow hazards around Building 615 entrances to facility
managers.
Electrically Powered Tools & Shop Equipment
Governing Directives: OSHA 29 CFR 1910; NFPA 70E; NFPA 101; DAFMAN 91-203.
Controls: Inspect all portable tools and cords before use for broken pins, frayed cords, or cracked casings. Never defeat ground pins or
daisy-chain power strips/surge protectors. Personally owned electrical tools and appliances are prohibited without supervisor authorization.
Space heaters and high-draw breakroom appliances must be plugged directly into wall outlets, never into modular furniture or extension
cords.
Hazardous Chemicals & Hazard Communication (HAZCOM)
Governing Directives: AFI 90-821; 29 CFR 1910.1200; DAFMAN 91-203.
Controls: Review Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) for all dielectric oils, cable pulling lubricants, spray solvents, insulating varnishes, and battery
acids prior to handling. Ensure secondary containers have GHS-compliant labels displaying product identifier, hazard statements, signal
words, and pictograms. Use mandatory chemical-resistant PPE (nitrile/neoprene gloves, splash goggles, aprons).
Hazardous Energy Control (Lockout / Tagout - LOTO)
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203, Chapter 21; UFC 3-560-01.
Controls: Zero Energy State must be verified using the "Test-Before-Touch" principle with a calibrated, properly rated multimeter. Only
qualified Authorized Employees may perform LOTO. Use standardized locksets and AF Form 983 (Danger - Equipment Lockout Tag) or AF
Form 979 (Danger Tag). Never remove another worker's lock or tag without following the formal emergency removal procedure approved by
the Section Chief/Squadron Commander.
